# Tests GOSTDMODULE: when enabled, the standard library module is treated like
# a normal module, resolving its dependencies through the module cache and
# GOPROXY instead of the GOROOT/src/vendor directory.

env GO111MODULE=on
env GOPROXY=off

[!compiler:gc] skip

# GOSTDMODULE is a known configuration variable.
go env GOSTDMODULE
stdout '^$'

# By default, within the std module, dependencies resolve from GOROOT/src/vendor.
cd $GOROOT/src
go list -deps -f '{{.ImportPath}}' net/http
stdout ^vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack$
! stdout ^golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack$

# With GOSTDMODULE enabled, the import is no longer rewritten to the vendor
# directory; it resolves as a real module path. With GOPROXY=off and the module
# absent from the cache, resolution fails, but crucially it fails referring to
# the real module path rather than the vendored one.
env GOSTDMODULE=1
! go list -deps -f '{{.ImportPath}}' net/http
stderr golang.org/x/net
! stderr vendor[/\\]golang.org[/\\]x[/\\]net
